mbm-0068.clue: My best throw never touched the ground.
mbm-0068.quote: I floated a red disc over the hedge. The neighbor’s clothesline caught it between two white shirts. It hung there like a sunset until she took the washing in.

mbm-0069.clue: I keep a safety pin on the collar.
mbm-0069.quote: The heel came off my dancing shoe in the middle of our song. I kicked the other shoe under the bench and finished in my bright orange socks. The DJ played an encore.

mbm-0070.clue: My thumb made the little hollow.
mbm-0070.quote: I threw a bowl for cherries and left a dent in the rim by accident. Dad tried it that night and declared it a very fine place to rest a spoon. I kept the dent in the next three.

mbm-0071.clue: Look at this single white stone.
mbm-0071.quote: I had almost packed away the baduk set when my aunt placed one white stone back on the board. We played the whole corner all over again standing in our coats.

mbm-0072.clue: There’s a patch shaped like a teacup.
mbm-0072.quote: When my friend moved out, we made her a quilt from our mismatched kitchen towels. I gave the teacup a real little handle. That’s where she hooks her glasses at night.

mbm-0073.clue: The coat-check lady knows my tune.
mbm-0073.quote: I hum in line because I can never remember a song’s name. On Saturday the coat-check lady finished it for me, phoned the DJ, and sent me running to the floor.

mbm-0074.clue: I brought a pencil for the summit.
mbm-0074.quote: There’s a wooden box with a notebook at the top of our hill. The page was full, so I drew the view inside the back cover. Somebody came later and put a tiny kite in my sky.

mbm-0075.clue: The trail map fits inside my mitten.
mbm-0075.quote: I sat on the first chairlift with my little brother and named each run after a soup. He still asks to ski Tomato before lunch. I know just the slope he means.

mbm-0076.clue: I use my old postcard for one color.
mbm-0076.quote: I took a watercolor set down to the harbor to match the blue in a faded postcard. By the time I mixed it, the sun had come out and given the water a thousand silver freckles.

mbm-0077.clue: Listen for the squeak and then the pause.
mbm-0077.quote: I spent an hour scanning a pine tree for a squeaky bird. It was a rusty swing behind me. A robin was sitting on the chain, watching me search.

mbm-0078.clue: My gym bag has an oven mitt in it.
mbm-0078.quote: The paint on my first kettlebell chipped, so my sister sewed it a quilted cover for the trip home. The handle sticks out like the neck of a very stout teapot.

mbm-0079.clue: I count the bells even when I miss one.
mbm-0079.quote: At noon in a town I’d never visited, I followed the bell sound straight into a clock repair shop. Every clock struck a minute apart. The owner gave me a chair for the full concert.

mbm-0080.clue: We pass the baton at the mailbox.
mbm-0080.quote: Dad can’t do the whole hill now. He jogs the first block with a rolled newspaper, hands it to me at the blue mailbox, and waits for my finishing headline.

mbm-0081.clue: I left the paddle in the bow on purpose.
mbm-0081.quote: I let my canoe drift on the last stretch home. A dragonfly landed on the spare paddle and stayed through two bends in the river. All passengers deserve a quiet ride.

mbm-0082.clue: We use the biscuit tin for the bank.
mbm-0082.quote: My cousin paid rent with a biscuit crumb by mistake. Our youngest player took it very seriously and issued change in sprinkles. The bank has needed a lid ever since.

mbm-0083.clue: This square opens like a window.
mbm-0083.quote: My first apartment had a beautiful view of a brick wall. I stitched it into a quilt with a little curtain you can lift. Behind it I put the sea.

mbm-0084.clue: The orange stripe came from the grocer.
mbm-0084.quote: I ran out of orange halfway through painting the market. The grocer sat me down with a tangerine to peel while I mixed the color. I left the spiral peel in the picture.

mbm-0085.clue: The center is all wrong when you look straight down.
mbm-0085.quote: I turned the middle square of my quilt by mistake. From the stairs it looked like a spinning windmill, so I turned the next three as well. Best view in the house.

mbm-0086.clue: There’s a tea strainer in my bag.
mbm-0086.quote: I hit a practice ball into our rain barrel. My aunt fished it out with the long tea strainer and bowed. She’s the only person I know who takes a curtain call for a water hazard.

mbm-0087.clue: Guess who sat for this portrait.
mbm-0087.quote: I stitched my own face into a lap quilt for Mum. Our cat sleeps across the hair. At last I know what I’d look like in a very furry hat.

mbm-0088.clue: We put on good slippers for the opening theme.
mbm-0088.quote: My sister grew out of her moon-and-stars pajamas, so we made them into cushions for mystery night. When the clues get scary she hugs the moon and I hide behind the stars.

mbm-0089.clue: I can pick out our dock from the middle of the lake.
mbm-0089.quote: My aunt ties a red tea towel to the post whenever she watches me ski. I come in slow enough to see her wave it. Then I wave the lake water out of my ears.

mbm-0090.clue: The cracked one sounds the best.
mbm-0090.quote: I went to the thrift shop for a lamp and came home with three teacups. One sings a perfect high note when I tap the rim. The shopkeeper threw in a spoon so I could prove it.

mbm-0091.clue: My bell came from a child’s bicycle.
mbm-0091.quote: I rode along the canal with my grandfather’s old duck-shaped bike bell. At the first bridge I rang it and a real duck answered. We stopped for a proper introduction.

mbm-0092.clue: My ticket has a triangle folded into it.
mbm-0092.quote: We used to fold the corners of our dance tickets when the band played our favorite song. I still have one night with all four corners turned down. My calves remember it too.
